approval_required_for: Selection among multiple plausible exact sample-project wrapper or app-shell targets after bounded evidence collection.
Any architecture, pipeline structure, memory layout, numeric policy or tolerance, floorplan-policy, or major template change proposed by a repair.

Starting a new semantic-identity epoch because checkpoint, stimulus, target-model reference, testbench contract, or exact board-wrapper sources must change; such a restart invalidates current-layer and higher-layer evidence.

Any repair that exceeds the trusted bounded-template or generated-integration boundary. Applying the recorded framework loose defaults for initially absent atol, rtol, or max_mismatch_fraction before DUT output is examined does not require approval.

executable_actions.on_failure: Do not promote the aggregate. Emit the dependency-blocked manifest and return each missing or conflicting edge, tool name, checker name, or action contract to the named owning specialist; do not fabricate a replacement refinement.
produces: artifact.stage6.dependency_blocked_manifest if any required specialist input is unresolved
executable_actions.rationale: Consume rather than recreate every specialist decision, add explicit non-bypass backend edges, prove acyclicity and materialization coverage, and produce the checker-bound Stage7/backend handoff.

executable_actions.on_failure: Block every single-layer, board, and backend consumer. Re-run current-contract validation or repair the validator/identity binding; never infer validity from the existing Stage7 ready outcomes.
produces: artifact.stage6.downstream_artifact_blocklist updated for stale leaf and single-layer certificates
executable_actions.rationale: Artifact presence and historical pass status are insufficient. Bind reuse to the current semantic contract and select the earliest invalid hierarchical scope.

consumes: generated DUT weight-loader and tensor-binding manifests
executable_actions.on_failure: Block operator execution. Repair the target-model reference runner, catalog, loader binding, numeric-policy resolver, or semantic harness; do not use random, RTL-derived, identity/default, sampled-weight, or model-tail golden data. If current-run tolerances are absent, apply only the authorized frozen framework loose defaults before DUT output is inspected.
executable_actions.rationale: Create independent expected outputs and immutable identity evidence before any DUT functional pass. Randomness may generate only the input stimulus; expected values must come from executing the real target Transformer blocks.

executable_actions.on_failure: Block single_transformer_layer and invoke stage7.localize_repair_and_rerun_current_layer with layer=operator_leaf_modules and the failed real-tool outputs. Do not promote a partial leaf set.
executable_actions.rationale: Re-establish a current-contract certificate for every spatial operator leaf before connecting a Transformer layer.

consumes: failed current-layer real-tool logs and wave/trace evidence
exact board-wrapper source hash manifest when layer=board_axi_ddr_wrapped_system
executable_actions.on_failure: Keep the current and all higher layers blocked. If the evidence identifies a missing checker/reference capability, repair that capability rather than claiming hardware failure. If repair requires architecture, pipeline, memory-layout, numeric-policy/tolerance, major-template, checkpoint, stimulus, reference, testbench-contract, or exact-wrapper identity changes, stop and request the corresponding approval/backtrack instead of applying the change.
produces: stage backtrack request when a higher-layer trace contradicts a lower-layer boundary
executable_actions.rationale: Convert an actual simulator/checker failure into an earliest-causal boundary, compact repair context, bounded template repair, and same-layer rerun while preserving semantic identities.

executable_actions.on_failure: Block every multi-layer, AXI/DDR, and backend node. Invoke stage7.localize_repair_and_rerun_current_layer with layer=single_transformer_layer_kernel; do not skip to the board wrapper.
executable_actions.rationale: Connect only currently certified operator leaves into one Transformer-layer kernel and verify value, shape, order, liveness, numeric, and weight-binding behavior before board integration.

executable_actions.on_failure: Block functional_sim. If supplied sources do not yield one evidence-backed wrapper/interface selection, emit a bounded ambiguity diagnosis and invoke stage7.resolve_ambiguous_target_with_approval; never guess a top, board, module, or path name and never substitute a simplified wrapper.
executable_actions.rationale: Discover and bind the exact user-supplied sample-project wrapper and source hashes, then materialize the multi-layer and AXI/DDR simulation contract without framework-core hardcoding or simplified substitutes.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep functional simulation or the affected backend gate blocked. Preserve all candidate evidence and request a new bounded decision; do not fall back to a framework default target.
executable_actions.rationale: Handle multiple plausible sample-project or app-shell targets through cited evidence and an explicit human boundary rather than a guessed integration name.

executable_actions.on_failure: Block every third-layer classifier and all backend nodes. Route actual liveness/value/order/protocol evidence to stage7.localize_repair_and_rerun_current_layer with layer=board_axi_ddr_wrapped_system. If the runner or analyzer lacks required evidence fields, classify and repair it as a verifier capability failure, not as hardware correctness.
executable_actions.rationale: Produce exactly one canonical board-wrapped simulation run to which every dynamic third-layer classifier is bound.

executable_actions.on_failure: Invalidate all classifier results from that canonical run and block board semantic aggregation. Localize the earliest causal boundary from the shared traces, repair only the bounded cause, rerun functional_sim, and regenerate every classifier from the new canonical run; do not mix old and new run evidence.
executable_actions.rationale: Derive all third-layer verdicts from the same canonical simulator run identifier, immutable identity closure, raw traces, and target-model reference.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep Vivado synthesis and every later backend/deployment gate blocked. Repair a missing checker/reference field as verifier evidence; otherwise invoke the board-layer localization and repair loop. Do not infer eligibility from individual classifier passes.
executable_actions.rationale: Promote the third repair-loop layer only when exact-wrapper identity, canonical simulation, all classifiers, independent reference outputs, frozen numeric policy, and complete Transformer-block weight consumption agree.

executable_actions.on_failure: Do not start synthesis. Update target_discovery_policy from cited sample-project/tool evidence; if multiple plausible targets remain, invoke the approval-bound ambiguity action instead of guessing.
executable_actions.rationale: Bind backend/app-shell targets from the exact sample project and cited evidence only after board semantic eligibility exists, while allowing later Vivado diagnostics to refine the policy.

executable_actions.on_failure: Block implementation. Feed real Vivado diagnostics into bounded backend recovery and target_discovery_policy refinement; if the target remains ambiguous, require approval rather than trying remembered or guessed names.
executable_actions.rationale: Run synthesis only after board semantic and backend target-selection certificates are valid; this is a downstream planned gate and is not claimed by Stage6.

executable_actions.on_failure: Block runtime bitstream, ABI, and board runtime. Route implementation diagnostics to bounded backend repair; require approval before any architecture, pipeline, memory-layout, floorplan-policy, or major-template change.
executable_actions.rationale: Run implementation, route, DRC, and final timing only after successful synthesis and continuing board-semantic eligibility.

executable_actions.on_failure: Block ABI and board runtime. Preserve implementation and wrapper hashes, then drive the next decision from bitstream/app-shell diagnostics; do not substitute another shell or wrapper.
executable_actions.rationale: Generate the runtime/app-shell bitstream only from the implemented design, exact sample wrapper identity, and valid board-semantic certificate.

executable_actions.on_failure: Block board runtime. Localize whether the mismatch is in generated runtime metadata, instrumentation, integration binding, or an approval-bound memory-layout change; never alter the golden or tolerance.
executable_actions.rationale: Cross-check the produced bitstream against the register map, DDR image, transfer units, memory layout, and runtime configuration before programming the board.

executable_actions.on_failure: Do not claim final closure. Preserve board logs and captures, localize the earliest runtime, ABI, memory, protocol, or value boundary, and route the evidence to bounded backend recovery or the three-layer backtrack mechanism as indicated.
executable_actions.rationale: Program and run the exact board/app-shell system only after bitstream and ABI gates, then validate Transformer-block outputs against the same immutable target-model reference.

observations: The visible 36-node graph admits the declared topological phase order. Independent roots converge at operator-leaf semantic evidence, then proceed through exactly one connected Transformer-layer semantic gate, the multi-layer/AXI-DDR wrapper gates, one canonical functional simulation, the third-layer classifiers, board semantic aggregation, and backend/deployment gates. No reverse dependency or cycle is visible.

case_multilayer_functional, case_pipeline_deadlock_check, case_axi_protocol_check, and case_ddr_image_roundtrip each directly depend on functional_sim. case_board_semantic_evidence depends on functional_sim and all four classifiers, preventing classifier-only or smoke-only promotion.

case_vivado_synthesis directly depends on case_board_semantic_evidence. Implementation, bitstream, ABI, and board runtime are transitively downstream through synthesis. The merged DAG should additionally bind every one of those nodes directly to case_board_semantic_evidence and the backend-eligibility certificate so a scheduler cannot bypass the semantic boundary through stale intermediate artifacts.

The current validator reports current_contract_valid=false and reuse_allowed=false for both artifact.stage7.operator_leaf_promotion_certificate and artifact.stage7.single_layer_promotion_certificate; the board certificate is absent. Historical Stage7 ready outcomes therefore do not authorize reuse under spatialaccagent.real_weight_semantic_evidence.v2. Stage7 must restart at operator_leaf_closure.

Stale current-stage certificates are downstream-consumption blockers, not independent blockers to approving a refined Stage6 contract that explicitly routes to the earliest invalid scope. They must remain immutable historical records rather than being overwritten by retry candidates.
The populated sacg_memory_truth reports zero active contamination barriers and zero open retry/backtrack requests. No historical record is being promoted to a current SACG-memory blocker.
Current Stage6 checker results are static-plan evidence with execution_status=not_applicable. They do not prove functional simulation, synthesis, implementation, bitstream, ABI, or board runtime.

The accelerator acceptance boundary is Transformer blocks only. A complete checkpoint tensor catalog may retain hashes for source integrity, but DUT weight-consumption coverage and expected-output boundaries must use an explicit Transformer-block required-tensor subset and exclude embedding/tokenization, final model norm, LM head/logits, and sampling.

The numeric binding is visible, but detailed atol, rtol, and max_mismatch_fraction values are not exposed in this role slice. Stage7 must select current-run values if present, otherwise apply the authorized frozen framework loose defaults before examining DUT output; the resulting policy must remain immutable throughout repair.

The role slice and state index do not expose the four named specialist refinement artifacts as independently consumable rows. This is a merge-materialization concern, not proof that their full-store content is absent. The final aggregate must resolve them through artifact.stage6.refinement_manifest and must not reconstruct or silently rewrite specialist decisions.
proposed_actions: Materialize the merged Stage6 DAG only after resolving every named specialist refinement through the refinement manifest, then rerun the complete static/checker audit.
Use current certificate validation to select operator_leaf_closure as the next Stage7 execution scope; preserve stale certificates as non-reusable historical evidence.

Prepare one immutable semantic identity bundle containing complete checkpoint hashes, deterministic input provenance, independent target-model Transformer-block boundary outputs, frozen numeric tolerances, semantic-testbench hashes, and bound-loader requirements.

Execute and promote strictly in three layers: all operator leaves, one connected Transformer layer, then the exact-sample-wrapper AXI/DDR system. Route every failure through tool evidence, CCTG/boundary localization, bounded repair, and same-layer rerun.
Emit one canonical board functional-simulation run manifest and require every third-layer classifier to consume that exact run identifier and hashes.

Issue the backend downstream-boundary certificate as blocked until case_board_semantic_evidence passes. Afterward run target discovery, synthesis, implementation, bitstream, ABI, and board runtime sequentially without treating their planned status as evidence.
risks: Current-stage merge risk: consuming only the visible canonical summary without the operator-leaf, single-layer, board-AXI/DDR, and certificate-validation specialist artifacts would violate the team aggregation contract and could hide a specialist disagreement.
Certificate-contamination risk: a selector that keys on artifact presence or historical Stage7 status instead of current_contract_valid could incorrectly skip the operator and single-layer reruns.

Cross-layer identity risk: classifiers or semantic aggregators could accidentally consume outputs from different simulator runs, DUT revisions, checkpoints, stimuli, numeric tolerances, testbench hashes, weight loaders, or wrapper source hashes unless a single canonical run identifier and complete hash closure are mandatory.

Scope risk: wording such as complete checkpoint can be misinterpreted as requiring model-tail tensors to be consumed by the DUT. The merged contract must distinguish checkpoint catalog integrity from the Transformer-block-only DUT required-tensor set.

Downstream integration risk: sample-project wrapper or app-shell target discovery may be ambiguous. The system must cite the supplied project sources and real tool diagnostics, request bounded approval when multiple targets remain plausible, and never guess or substitute a simplified wrapper.

Repair-boundary risk: a liveness, value, order, address, or protocol failure could trigger symptom patching or an unauthorized pipeline, memory-layout, architecture, numeric-policy, or major-template change unless earliest-boundary localization and approval boundaries are enforced.

case_operator_leaf_semantic_evidence -> case_tb_scaffold -> single_transformer_layer -> case_single_layer_functional -> case_single_layer_golden_compare -> case_single_layer_semantic_evidence
functional_sim + all four third-layer classifiers + immutable identities -> case_board_semantic_evidence
failed current-layer tool output -> failure_slice_localization -> targeted_replay -> causal_repair_context_pack -> bounded repair -> same-layer checker rerun
contradicting higher-layer boundary trace -> explicit targeted lower-layer backtrack request; no silent reopening
